name: pulse
title: Pulsing heart
summary: A heart drawn with pathExpression that pulses once a second: its scale and alpha follow a sine of continuousSec().
prompt: Draw a heart that beats: it grows, shrinks and fades in a loop once a second.
teaches: Loop an animation with sin(continuousSec() * 6.2832): one cycle per second, and continuousSec() makes the player repaint every frame
Scale a shape about its centre: draw it around the origin, then save, translate to the centre and scale(sx, sy)
Fade with the same clock through a paint alpha expression
Centre with translate(componentWidth() / 2, componentHeight() / 2) and fold min(componentWidth(), componentHeight()) / 200 into the pulse scale so the heart fits any box

snippets.note: paint alpha 0.65 ± 0.35 from the same sine
the heart curve: x = 64 sin³t, y from four cosines

check.describe: At a quarter past a whole second (continuousSec() = n + 0.25) the heart is at its largest and brightest; at n + 0 it is mid-size and two-thirds opaque; at n + 0.75 small and dim. Resized, the heart stays centred and scales with the shorter side.

pitfalls: Drive a looping animation with continuousSec(), not animationTime(): an expression that only reads animationTime() never schedules a repaint, so the document is drawn once and stays still (EXAMPLES_FINDINGS U6)
continuousSec() is the second within the hour with milliseconds (0–3600): it jumps back to 0 on the hour, harmless for a sine with a whole-second period
To pin a frame for a screenshot pin the clock with milliseconds (epoch ms); animation_time does not move continuousSec()
Alpha is 0–1 in a paint alpha expression, not 0–255
